title: The psycho-social influence of lighting. an experimental proof of concept
research_question: Could different lighting design conditions influence individuals in terms of environmental atmosphere perception and lighting appearance? Could different lighting design conditions influence individuals in terms of social appraisal, prospect evaluation, and sociability?

participants.description: 20 voluntary participants (5 males, 15 females) divided into 10 couples (5 male/female, 5 female/female). 5 unacquainted couples and 5 acquainted ones. Ages ranged from 21 to 34 years old (M = 23.7, SD = 5.57). Nationality: 80% Italian, 10% Pakistani, 5% from Montenegro, 5% Egyptian. Healthy individuals, wore visual aids if needed.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: A full-scale laboratory room (4m x 6m, 2.9m height) with white walls/ceiling and medium grey floor (20% light reflectance). Windows obscured. A prototypal LED-based lighting fixture provided four alternative lighting conditions (C1-C4).
stimuli_or_exposures.source: Description of the experimental room, LED lighting prototype and lighting conditions alternatives sections

stimuli_or_exposures.description: C1: Direct-indirect Cold CCT (Eh=536 lux, CCT@Eh=5400K, Eeye=35 lux, CCT@Eeye=4487K). C2: Direct-indirect Warm CCT (Eh=387 lux, CCT@Eh=2960K, Eeye=24 lux, CCT@Eeye=2927K). C3: Direct Warm CCT (Eh=370 lux, CCT@Eh=2958K, Eeye=16 lux, CCT@Eeye=2917K). C4: Direct Cold CCT (Eh=508 lux, CCT@Eh=5523K, Eeye=21 lux, CCT@Eeye=5096K).
stimuli_or_exposures.source: Table 1, LED lighting prototype and lighting conditions alternatives sections

findings.quote: The majority of mental activities were reported with cold direct/indirect (29%) and with warm direct/indirect lighting conditions (33%), presumably indicating a preference for perceived higher brightness for visual performances.
tension and anxiety-provoking activities were evoked prevalently (35%) under cold lighting conditions (C1-C4).

findings.mechanism: linked to concentration (positive mood) and tenseness (negative mood)
findings.quote: Cold CCT evoked high-level visual task activities (31% with C1 and 28% with C4) and inspired ones linked both to concentration (positive mood) and tenseness (negative mood).
The lighting condition of warm direct/indirect lighting (C2) evoked more leisure activities (45%)

findings.consequent: Evoked more relaxing activities (low-level visual tasks)
findings.quote: warm, direct lighting (C3) evoked more relaxing activities (56%), which were both low-level visual tasks (41%).
Warm CCT elicited socialisation activities: 29% with the direct/indirect lighting condition C2 and 35% with the direct lighting condition C3

mechanisms: Lighting sends visual messages influencing affective, cognitive, associative and motivational ways.
Luminance distribution and lighting levels send consistent visual messages that define the impression of a space that socially includes or excludes.
Lighting allows environmental cognition and influences impression and affective evaluation of atmospheres.
Lighting influences the brain by sending visual messages which may involve thinking (cognitive process), emotions (affective process) in addition to motivation and purposeful behaviours.
implementation_implications: Appropriate lighting design strategies are necessary to support the social dimension in socio-spatial contexts where collaboration and socialisation are essential for overall quality of life.
Lighting may be adjusted to support different social relationships to negotiate the impression of space and improve sociability during conversation.
Warm white lighting defines a more relaxing atmosphere and creates a more sociable and favourable impression for socialization compared to cold white lighting.
Cold white lighting is considered unsociable and unfavourable for socialization, and evokes activities connected to concentration and high-level visual tasks.

Direct/indirect lighting contributes to a positive impression of luminous atmosphere, providing a visually clean, brighter, and livelier environment, preferred for enhancing conversation and inclusion.
Direct lighting conditions isolate individuals, creating a more private and confined environment suitable for relaxing and solitary activities.
Non-uniform lighting (direct lighting) may be used to virtually separate individuals for individual, mental, and concentrated activities and to enhance territorialization.
Uniform lighting (direct/indirect lighting) may be employed to increase prospect, enhance cohesion, collaboration, and socialisation.
Practical design guidance for architects, interior and lighting designers to develop new lighting design solutions that take into account psycho-social effects.

limitations: Study performed in a controlled laboratory setting, not a real-life context, limiting generalizability to real socio-spatial contexts.
Results cannot be generalized to the overall population in different age ranges (only 21-34 years old).
Unbalanced distribution of nationalities (majority Italian) did not permit analysis of social influence of lighting among different cultures.
